12. The learned trial court during deciding the fate of the suit after framing use different issues held that in the original suit there is no defect of party and the suit as framed is maintainable. The plaintiffs are entitled to get an order of partition but the area of the land would he five decimals instead of 7(seven) decimals of land. It was further held by the trial court that exhibit-1(ka) which is prior to the transfer deed in favour of plaintiffs' predecessor was duly effected and the transferor owner of the land delivered possession from suit plot No.9093. The boundary of the transferred property which is cited within the content of the deed has been reflected within the averments of the witnesses as adduced from the sides of the parties. The learned court below in his findings and decision consulting the title documents of the parties arrived at a conclusive decision that the plot No. 9093 from where the defendants are possessing consists of an area 8might) decimals and the total quantum of land of the said plot as it appears from the settlement record that 43 decimals had been owned and possessed by the vendor prior to his transfer. After transfer of 38 decimals and 08(eight) decimals the property left behind cannot be more than 05(five) decimals of land and as such the boundaries which is properly described within the testimony of the witnesses makes it clear that the defendants do possess their purchased land after constructing their dwelling but and boundary wall which is admitted from the plaintiffs witnesses. The observation and findings which is cited within the contents of the judgment in deciding the issue No.3 was not properly addressed by the lower appellate court in the impugned judgment and decree. In this context; the learned Advocate on behalf of the petitioners argued that under the purview of Order XLI rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure it is the mandatory duty of the appellate court to rebut the findings of the trial court adverting evidence on records in the case of reversal of the decision but in the instant case apparently the lower appellate court violating the provisions of law in a evasive manner decided the fate of the suit as well as ' appeal which is an apparent error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 15. It is a settled principle of law that the lower appellate court being final court of fact will have to discuss and assess the evidence on record independently while either reversing or affirming the finding to the trial Court. In case of reversal it is more incumbent upon the appellate Court to re-assess the evidence on record and to arrive at his own independent finding. In the instant case the specific findings in support of decision of the trial Court have not been reversed by the lower appellate Court exercising its power under Order XLI. rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Having regard to the facts, circumstances and discussions referred to above I am constrained to hold such a view that the submissions given from the side of the petitioners have got every nexus in the instant case and substance and the impugned judgment and decree inasmuch as suffers from material illegality as well as irregularity and there has been glaring misconception of law and non-consideration of material facts as well as evidence on records causing an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice the impugned judgment and decree is not sustainable.
